title: Colby vs Wesleyan: tuition, size, location
summary: Colby College (Colby) versus Wesleyan University (Wesleyan). Also searched as Wesleyan vs Colby. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Wesleyan University and Colby College are both private nonprofit institutions, as indicated by their ownership codes in the College Scorecard. Wesleyan University, located in Middletown, has an undergraduate enrollment of 3,067 students, while Colby College in Waterville enrolls 2,407 undergraduates. The tuition for in-state students at Wesleyan is $70,342, slightly higher than Colby's $69,600. These differences highlight variations in size, location, and cost between Wesleyan vs Colby.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing the cost of attendance, Wesleyan University and Colby College have similar tuition rates for both in-state and out-of-state students. Wesleyan charges $70,342 for tuition regardless of residency status, while Colby's tuition is slightly lower at $69,600. Regarding student debt, the median debt for Wesleyan graduates who completed their programs is $17,000, which is somewhat less than Colby's median debt of $19,157. These figures provide insight into the financial commitments associated with attending each institution, reflecting minor differences in tuition and graduate debt between Wesleyan vs Colby.

sections.heading: Pick Wesleyan if
paragraphs: Pick Wesleyan if you prefer a private nonprofit university with a competitive admission rate of approximately 16.5%.
